recap.takeaways:
1) ZWIFT FTP DRIFT — AND THE GOOD NEWS IS BURIED INSIDE IT: those eight minutes were enough to take the measurement. The check reads, verbatim: "DRIFT: Zwift appears to have executed at FTP ~226 W, but the pipeline assumes 236 W (-4.3%). Fix Zwift's FTP to 236 W and decline its auto-detect prompt." Confidence high, off 440 samples inside rep 1. Do it before tomorrow. Tomorrow's reference block pins ftpOverride, so the 165 W target itself is safe either way — but the desync figure is the thing the verdict step refuses to carry once it is older than three days, and tomorrow now inherits one at age one day. The single load-bearing job this ride had, it did in its first eight minutes.

2) ADAPT — CCI5 CLASSIFIED FAILED, ABSORBED, NOTHING MOVED. Cause is not established and I am not going to invent one. Rep 1 gives no physiological reason to stop: in-band power, heart rate five under threshold, coupled, no drift signal anywhere in it. That argues against "the prescription was too hard" rather than for it. With no note on the day and no effort rating on the ride, circumstance and plain appetite for the session are both live and I cannot separate them from here. Rule applied: lost time is absorbed, not chased — nothing is bolted onto Wednesday or Thursday. And the remedy the rule would normally ask for after a failed hard session, an easy day in front of the next one, is already built into this week: Friday carries no endurance at all, so Saturday's RCI3 still gets the freshest legs in the block. No plan edit was needed; the absorption is documented in WEEK_14_PLAN.md.

3) WHAT IT COSTS, IN ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN ARGUMENT. 24 of the week's 32 bike-threshold minutes did not happen, so the week's two hard stimuli are effectively down to one — Saturday's RCI3. Unlike Monday's lost easy hour, this loss is roughly half hard and half easy, so it does not push the easy ratio further under the floor. And the item this week actually protects is untouched: tomorrow's CF10 and its reference block.

4) THE GYM WAS THE STRONGEST THING ON THE DAY. Pushdown swept 12 on all four sets at 100, so the next straight pushdown session goes to 110. Chest fly held the floor of the range on its first session at 45. Incline press improved on every set at 70. One to watch rather than act on: lateral raise came back 12/11/11/11 and three of those sit at the plan's written fallback line. That rule reads across all eight of the week's sets, so Friday's four decide it — the load does not move tonight.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.

mob.name: Deadbugs + bodyweight glute bridges
mob.when: at the end of the gym visit, before you leave
mob.desc: Deadbugs with the low back pinned flat, then bodyweight glute bridges. 3 of 3 this week. Bodyweight only — nothing here needs the gym, so it survives a rushed morning.

mob.name: 90/90 hip lift with full exhale
mob.desc: 5 breaths × 2–3 sets. Needs a floor and nothing else, so travel changes nothing. Not within ~90 minutes of a large meal.

2026-09-12.mind: Four by eight minutes at 4:22 to 4:42 per kilometre, in a place I do not know, off a full day with nothing in it — pacing that so rep four still exists is a skill, and getting deliberately better at a hard thing is the point.

end.name: RCI3 — 64′ (4 × 8′ Z3)
end.detail: This gets the freshest legs of the week and that is not an accident: Friday carries no endurance and no leg-heavy class work, so this is the only hard session in the block that starts from a genuine rest day. It is the one good thing the travel constraint bought.
end.desc:
5′ Z1 @ 5:45–7:17/km, 5′ Z2 @ 5:01–5:45/km, 4 × (8′ Z3 @ 4:22–4:42/km / 3′ Z1), 5′ Z2, 5′ Z1. (Verified 2026-08-30.)
Thirty-two minutes of threshold running — the largest block of hard time in the week. Eight minutes is long enough that pacing decides everything: go out at 4:22 and rep four will not exist. Open rep 1 at the slow end of the band and let it come to you.
If the route is unfamiliar or hilly, run the reps on heart rate (Z3 = 161–167) rather than fighting the pace band on terrain. Rolling-terrain scatter is the ground, not an execution fault.
It travels — shoes and a road.

mob.name: Hip flexors — half-kneeling + couch stretch
mob.when: right after the run, while you are still warm
mob.desc: 2 × 45–60 s per side each. Squeeze the down-side glute FIRST, then lean — the tuck is the exercise, not the lean. No class tomorrow morning, so nothing is compromised by it.

mob.name: 90/90 hip lift with full exhale
mob.desc: 5 breaths × 2–3 sets. Full exhale is the whole exercise. Not within ~90 minutes of a large meal.

2026-09-13.mind: Three ten-minute blocks at 5:01 to 5:45 with the rest genuinely slow, which is a harder discipline than running fast — hours like this are what make me the one who still says yes to the long day out with Fleur in twenty years.

end.name: RAe1 — 60′ aerobic-interval run
end.detail: READ THE STRUCTURE BEFORE YOU RUN IT. RAe1 is the SMALLEST workout in the RAe family — nothing like week 13's RAe10. Only 30 of the 60 minutes are Zone 2. Closing the week on the smaller of the two runs is deliberate: it leaves week 15 opening on a clean Monday.
end.desc:
10′ Z1 @ 5:45–7:17/km, 3 × (10′ Z2 @ 5:01–5:45/km / 3′ Z1), 10′ Z1. (Pulled live 2026-09-07.)
This is not an hour of Zone 2 — it is three ten-minute Z2 blocks inside twenty-nine minutes of Zone 1.
Finishing the last Z2 block and never coming back down turns the tail into Zone X, which is the classic way this session type goes wrong and the exact error RAe10 was flagged for.
The three-minute floats are short and that is the point. They are floats, not recoveries — so the Z2 blocks have to be genuinely Z2 rather than an assault.
(Segments sum to 59′ against the library's stated 60 — their rounding, not a missing segment.)
